task_title: P2 — node-create.sh never stages scripts/disk_floor.py, so every documented node creation dies with a bare python3 error on its first layer
task_criteria: CF-075 exists in .coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl with status pending and a non-empty probe field. The defect reproduces at the landed commit: grep -c disk_floor.py scripts/node-create.sh prints 0 while grep -c disk_floor.py scripts/project-node.sh prints 1, so the resolver the node entry point executes is never staged into the node node-create.sh builds. The end-to-end reproduction also holds: copy scripts/project-node.sh and scripts/lib.sh into one temp directory, copy scripts/harness/install-hermes.sh into harness/ beneath it, chmod +x the entry point, then run it with HOME set to an empty directory as project-node.sh --apply --project cfprobe --harness hermes --repo https://github.com/github/gitignore — it prints a python3 line naming disk_floor.py with No such file or directory, then NODE: FAIL (disk floor), and exits 1. The row acceptance criteria require node-create.sh to stage every file the entry point executes (derived, not hand-maintained), a named disk-floor row instead of a bare interpreter error, no live agent left behind after a failed provision, and a tests/selftest.sh fixture that proves both directions, with bash tests/selftest.sh printing SELFTEST: PASS at the landed commit. The lane measured this by creating a real node on a reachable bunker host: spawn PASS, staged PASS, then the same disk_floor.py error inside the node, FAIL provision, VERIFY FAIL, NODE INCOMPLETE (2), and the spawned agent was left alive until it was destroyed by hand.
